- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to capture mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; force a 3–7 day lagged correction based on sentiment reversal.
- For 30-day forecasts, model underperforms when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); use sentiment-weighted average of recent 7-day mean to anchor forecast.
- If sentiment is high but price is falling, model often ignores sentiment; force a 1–2 day lagged sentiment correction to avoid false optimism.
- When sentiment is low and price is rising, model often underreacts; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to capture sentiment-driven reversal.
